channel.title: Mostly Markets
channel.description: Why stocks moved, explained the same day.

item.title: KLA (KLAC) Tops Q1 Estimates as Chip-Inspection Sales Rise 29%
item.description: KLA's September-quarter revenue rose 29% to $4.14 billion, ahead of the $4.05 billion expected, and it guided to $4.7 billion for December. The stock rose 5.5% on Thursday.

item.title: Amphenol (APH) Tops Q3 Estimates as AI Datacom Sales More Than Double
item.description: Amphenol's sales rose 65% to $10.23 billion, beating the $9.44 billion expected, as IT datacom sales jumped 117%. The stock rose 3.5% on Wednesday and 1.4% on Thursday.

item.title: GE Vernova (GEV) Tops Q3 Estimates as Orders Nearly Double to $29 Billion
item.description: GE Vernova's revenue rose 27% to $12.64 billion, beating the $11.99 billion expected, as orders jumped 96%. The stock fell 1.9% on Wednesday, then rose 1.1% on Thursday.

item.title: Gilead (GILD) Tops Q3 Estimates as HIV Sales Grow 18%
item.description: Gilead's revenue rose 7% to $8.30 billion, beating the $7.81 billion expected, and it raised its 2026 sales forecast. The stock was up 3% after hours.

item.title: Merck (MRK) Tops Q3 Estimates as Keytruda and Gardasil Outperform
item.description: Merck's sales rose 5% to $18.09 billion, ahead of the $17.31 billion expected, and it raised its 2026 profit forecast. The stock rose 3.8% on Thursday.

item.title: Mastercard (MA) Tops Q3 Estimates as Value-Added Services Grow 19%
item.description: Mastercard's revenue rose 14% to $9.81 billion, ahead of the $9.63 billion expected, as services sales grew 19%. The stock jumped 4.2% to a 52-week closing high.

item.title: Shell (SHEL) Tops Q3 Estimates as Refining Margins Hit a Record
item.description: Shell's adjusted earnings nearly doubled to $10.81 billion, beating forecasts, and it raised its quarterly buyback to $5 billion. Its US shares rose 2.4% to $107.67.

item.title: Linde (LIN) Tops Q3 Estimates as Higher Prices Lift Sales 9%
item.description: Linde's adjusted EPS of $4.59 beat the $4.52 expected on sales of $9.4 billion, and it nudged up its 2026 forecast. The stock slipped 1.0% on Thursday.

item.title: Stocks Making the Biggest Moves After Hours: Intel, Reddit, Stryker, Pinterest and Amazon
item.description: Intel fell 19.6% after hours on a weak forecast, Reddit 16.7% on soft guidance and a traffic warning, and Amazon 6.5% after missing on profit and ads.

item.title: The Earnings Week Ahead: Apple, AMD and Palantir, Plus the Election and Jobs
item.description: Apple and Palantir report on Monday, AMD on Tuesday, and Arm and Qualcomm on Wednesday. In between come the midterm elections and, on Friday 6 November, the October jobs report.

item.title: AMD (AMD) Reports Earnings on Tuesday: What to Watch
item.description: AMD reports after the close on Tuesday, 3 November. Analysts expect revenue of about $13.1 billion, up 41%, and the forecast for its Helios AI servers may matter more.

item.title: What to Expect From Palantir's (PLTR) Q3 Earnings
item.description: Palantir reports after the close on Monday, 2 November. Analysts expect revenue of $2.17 billion to $2.18 billion, up about 84% and above the top of its own forecast.

item.title: What to Expect From Apple's (AAPL) Q4 Earnings
item.description: Apple reports after the close on Monday, 2 November. Analysts expect revenue of about $113 billion, up 10%, at the top of Apple's own forecast, with the stock at a record.

item.title: Chevron (CVX) Reports Earnings Tomorrow: What to Watch
item.description: Chevron reports before the open on Friday. Analysts expect adjusted EPS of $4.78, up from $1.85 a year ago, after a second quarter that beat estimates by 50 cents a share.

item.title: Stock Market Today: Alphabet's Record Drop Pulls the Nasdaq Down 1.4%
item.description: The Nasdaq fell 1.38% and the S&P 500 0.30% as Alphabet had its worst day since its 2004 listing, while small caps rose 1.0%. Amazon and Intel slid after hours.

item.title: Exxon Mobil (XOM) Reports Earnings Tomorrow: What to Watch
item.description: Exxon reports before the open on Friday. Analysts expect adjusted EPS of $3.90, double a year ago, and the company has flagged a $4.5 billion lift from refining.

item.title: What to Expect From Shopify's (SHOP) Q3 Earnings
item.description: Shopify reports before the open on Tuesday, 3 November. Analysts expect revenue of $3.70 billion to $3.74 billion, at least 30% more than a year ago, after a quarter that sent the stock up 17%.

item.title: What to Expect From Uber's (UBER) Q3 Earnings
item.description: Uber reports before the open on Wednesday, 4 November, with its stock down 19.5% this year. Analysts expect gross bookings of about $59.7 billion, in the upper half of its own forecast.

item.title: AbbVie (ABBV) Reports Earnings Tomorrow: What to Watch
item.description: AbbVie reports before the open on Friday. Analysts expect adjusted EPS of $3.74 to $3.79, at or above the $3.73 to $3.77 the company guided to after an 11-cent research charge.

item.title: Amazon (AMZN) Q3: AWS Speeds Up, but Ads and Profit Miss Estimates
item.description: AWS grew 39%, ahead of estimates, but Amazon missed on profit and ads and guided Q4 operating income below forecasts. The stock slid 4.4% after hours.

item.title: Intel (INTC) Q3: Profit Tops Estimates, Shares Plunge on a Weak Forecast
item.description: Intel beat on profit and grew data-center sales 78%, but guided Q4 revenue to $15.0-16.0 billion, short of the $17.07 billion expected. The stock fell 15.5% after hours.

item.title: Alphabet (GOOGL) Shares Plunge After Search Falls Short and Cash Burn Grows
item.description: Alphabet plunged 12.6% on Thursday, its worst day since its 2004 listing, after search revenue missed estimates and free cash flow came in at negative $9.07 billion.

item.title: Apple Leads the Magnificent Seven in 2026 as Alphabet Slides Into the Red
item.description: Apple is up 28.3% this year as of Thursday's close. Alphabet's 12.6% drop after its results left it down 9.3%, one of three of the seven now below where they started 2026.

item.title: Caterpillar (CAT) Beats Q3 Profit Estimates, but Shares Plunge on Its Outlook
item.description: Caterpillar earned $7.20 a share, above the $7.08 expected, but kept its 2026 sales forecast unchanged and warned of thin margins. The stock plunged 9.25%, its worst day since March 2020.

item.title: Eli Lilly (LLY) Tops Q3 Estimates as Mounjaro Sales Jump 65%
item.description: Lilly's revenue rose 39% to $24.40 billion, beating the $22.61 billion expected, and it raised its 2026 sales forecast by $5.5 billion. The stock jumped 6.6% to a record close.

item.title: Fortinet (FTNT) Shares Plunge After It Cuts Its Service Revenue Forecast
item.description: Fortinet plunged 20.1% on Thursday after cutting its 2026 service revenue forecast to $5.15-5.17 billion, below the $5.2 billion analysts expected, despite a Q3 beat.

item.title: Microsoft (MSFT) Shares Give Back Their After-Hours Gain as Investors Weigh Spending
item.description: Microsoft closed down 0.2% at $530.14 on Thursday, erasing a 4% after-hours jump, as investors looked past its earnings beat to capex $5.5 billion below estimates.

item.title: ServiceNow (NOW) Stock Has Its Worst Day on Record After a Soft Forecast
item.description: ServiceNow plunged 27.0% on Thursday after forecasting 18.5% growth in a key measure of future sales, slower than the 21% it just reported and below estimates.

item.title: Why Carvana (CVNA) Stock Is Soaring Today
item.description: Carvana soared 15.7% on Thursday after selling a record 217,385 cars in the third quarter, up 39%, with revenue of $8.04 billion ahead of estimates.

item.title: Stocks Making the Biggest Moves Yesterday: F5, Vertiv, Oracle, Alphabet and Sandisk
item.description: F5 plunged 20.4% on its forecast, Vertiv soared 16.5% and Oracle 10.7% on Wednesday, and Alphabet fell 10.8% after hours after its search revenue missed.

item.title: Microsoft (MSFT) Beats Q1 Estimates as Azure Growth Speeds Up to 48%
item.description: Microsoft rose 4.0% after hours as revenue of $92.28 billion beat the $90.69 billion expected and Azure grew 48%, above the company's own forecast.

item.title: The 10-Year Treasury Yield Has Spent Six Weeks Around 5%, a Level Last Seen in 2007
item.description: The 10-year closed at 5.05% on Wednesday after the Fed held rates. It has finished at 5% or higher on 26 of the last 31 trading days and peaked at 5.31%, the highest since 2002.

item.title: Alphabet (GOOGL) Q3: Cloud Sales Double, Stock Falls 11% After Hours
item.description: Alphabet fell 10.8% after hours as revenue of $127.58 billion just missed estimates, search fell short and free cash flow turned to a $9.07 billion outflow.

item.title: Stock Market Today: Stocks Edge Up After a Split Fed Vote as Oracle and Vertiv Soar
item.description: The S&P 500 rose 0.28% to 7,743.98 on Wednesday after the Fed held rates in a 10-2 vote. Oracle soared 10.7%, Vertiv 16.5%, and F5 plunged 20.4%.

item.title: F5 (FFIV) Shares Plunge After a Soft Forecast and a Piper Sandler Downgrade
item.description: F5 plunged 20.4% on Wednesday, the worst S&P 500 stock of the day, after forecasting 8% to 9% growth and lower margins, and Piper Sandler cut it to Neutral.

item.title: Oracle (ORCL) Shares Soar After It Sets a $225 Billion Revenue Target
item.description: Oracle soared 10.7% on Wednesday after its investor day targeted $225 billion or more in fiscal 2030 revenue and capped new outside funding at $20 billion.

item.title: Sandisk (SNDK) and Micron (MU) Shares Jump After SK Hynix's Record Quarter
item.description: Sandisk rose 7.7% and Micron 5.9% on Wednesday after SK hynix posted its first quarter above 100 trillion won in revenue and said memory demand will outrun supply through 2030.

item.title: Vertiv (VRT) Shares Soar as Its Orders More Than Double
item.description: Vertiv soared 16.5% on Wednesday, its best day since February, after its organic orders more than doubled and it raised its 2026 sales forecast by $650 million.

item.title: The Fed Held Rates, but Two Officials Wanted a Hike
item.description: The Fed kept its key rate at 3.75%-4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted another quarter-point increase.

item.title: 3 Beaten-Down Quality Stocks We Love and 1 We Hate
item.description: Adobe, Intuit and Booking sit 31% to 52% below their highs but still grow revenue by double digits and trade near 10 times free cash flow. Nike's 45% fall hasn't made it cheap.

item.title: Stocks Making the Biggest Moves Yesterday: Xylem, SoFi, Pentair, Celestica and Boeing
item.description: Xylem sank 14.2% on a forecast cut and Boeing 10.7% on a slower 737 ramp, while SoFi rose 13.4%, Pentair 12.8% and Celestica 12.1% on strong results on Tuesday.

item.title: Stock Market Today: Boeing's Slide Holds the Dow Flat as Chip Stocks Climb Again
item.description: The Nasdaq rose 1.18% as chip stocks gained 3.60% on a $63 billion financing deal for Anthropic, while Boeing's 10.7% drop left the Dow up just 15.99 points.

item.title: Visa (V) Beats Q4 Estimates, but Its 2027 Outlook Points to Slower Growth
item.description: Visa earned $3.48 a share on an adjusted basis, beating the $3.44 expected, on revenue up 13% to $12.1 billion, but guided to slower earnings growth in fiscal 2027.

item.title: Consumer Confidence Rebounded in October, but Inflation Worries Haven't Gone Away
item.description: The Conference Board's index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October, far above the 81.0 economists expected, as gas prices eased. Consumers still expect 5.8% inflation.

item.title: Boeing (BA) Shares Slide After It Delays Its 737 Production Ramp
item.description: Boeing plunged 10.7% on Tuesday, its worst day in at least five years, after it pushed its 737 ramp into late 2027 and forecast about $3 billion of free cash flow next year.

item.title: General Motors (GM) Shares Jump After It Moves Its Listing to the Nasdaq
item.description: GM rose 5.5% on Tuesday, its best day since January, after saying it will move its stock listing from the NYSE to the Nasdaq on 17 November, making it eligible for the Nasdaq-100.

item.title: Xylem (XYL) Shares Slide After It Cuts Its 2026 Forecast
item.description: Xylem plunged 14.2% on Tuesday, its worst day in at least five years, after the water-technology company cut its 2026 earnings forecast to $5.40 to $5.45 a share.

item.title: 3 Cash Machine Stocks We Love and 1 We Hate
item.description: GoDaddy, Salesforce and Altria turn a third or more of their revenue into free cash and trade at 8 to 14 times it. Meta's AI spending cut its free cash flow by 36%.

item.title: Stocks Making the Biggest Moves Yesterday: Nu Holdings, Fair Isaac, Lumentum, MercadoLibre and DoorDash
item.description: Nu Holdings fell 17.0% and MercadoLibre 7.8% after Brazil's election, Fair Isaac lost 13.2% on a downgrade, and Lumentum gained 8.2% on Monday.

item.title: Coca-Cola (KO) Tops Q3 Estimates as Volume Grows Outside North America
item.description: Coca-Cola earned 91 cents a share on a comparable basis, beating the 88 cents expected, on revenue up 7% to $13.4 billion, and raised its 2026 profit forecast for a third straight quarter.

item.title: UPS (UPS) Tops Q3 Estimates as Revenue per Package Climbs
item.description: UPS earned $1.69 a share on an adjusted basis, beating the $1.63 analysts expected, on revenue up 6.7% to $22.9 billion, and raised its 2026 revenue forecast to about $92.6 billion.

item.title: Stock Market Today: Anthropic's IPO Filing Lifts Chip Stocks as Brazil Crashes
item.description: The S&P 500 rose 0.70% and chip stocks 2.82% after Anthropic's IPO filing revived the AI trade, while Brazil's main index had its worst day since March 2020.

item.title: DoorDash (DASH) Shares Slide on Report It Is in Talks to Buy Instacart
item.description: DoorDash fell 6.1% on Monday after The Wall Street Journal reported it is in advanced talks to buy delivery rival Instacart, in a deal Reuters valued at about $17 billion.

item.title: Nu Holdings (NU) and MercadoLibre (MELI) Shares Slide After Lula Wins in Brazil
item.description: Nu Holdings fell 17.0% and MercadoLibre 7.8% on Monday after President Lula won Brazil's runoff, unwinding bets on a Bolsonaro win. Brazil's main index fell 13.88%.

item.title: Why Fair Isaac (FICO) Stock Is Sinking Today
item.description: Fair Isaac plunged 13.2% on Monday, the S&P 500's worst performer, after Wells Fargo downgraded it over its decision to hold the price of its mortgage credit score at $10.

item.title: 3 AI Infrastructure Stocks We Love and 1 We Hate
item.description: Micron, Nvidia and Vertiv grow fast and keep the cash they make. CoreWeave more than doubled its revenue but burned $13.65 billion in a year building data centers.

item.title: Stock Market Today: Oil Hits Its Highest Since April and the Dow Drops 653 Points
item.description: The Dow fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, on Friday as Brent crude settled at $116.72 after more attacks on Saudi Arabia. The S&P 500 lost 0.52% for a second weekly loss.

item.title: US Crude Is Up 80% This Year Despite Giving Back Its Whole Spring Spike
item.description: US crude settled at $103.27 on Friday, up 79.9% from $57.42 at the end of 2025, after topping $105 in April and sliding to $69.50 by the end of June.

item.title: Five Stocks That Made News This Week: Zscaler, Hasbro, Lam Research, Meta and Moderna
item.description: Zscaler soared 23.0% this week as security stocks rallied and Hasbro 18.9% after raising its outlook, while Lam Research plunged 12.8% on a supply warning and Meta 9.4% on its AI spending.

item.title: AT&T (T) Shares Slide After Report SpaceX Is Seeking 80,000 Cell Sites
item.description: AT&T slid 8.0% and T-Mobile 7.7% on Friday after Bloomberg reported SpaceX is in talks for at least 80,000 US cell sites for a phone network. Crown Castle soared 9.1%.
